envelope.description: Give body.commit and body.summary real producers, with render assertions scoped to the plan-driven route

body.title: Give body.commit and body.summary real producers, with render assertions scoped to the plan-driven route
body.summary: Both fields are declared and already rendered (c4) but set by none of the three body writers (c2, c8, c10) — two dead branches. Read HEAD at persist time for body.commit; accept an optional summary on the validate input for body.summary. The WRITE side is route-agnostic and genuinely this task's job, but the RENDER assertions must be scoped to the PLAN-DRIVEN route only, because the standalone renderer emits neither section until t8 (c5) — an unscoped check would fail t7 for a reason t7 cannot fix, and t7 is ordered before t8. Standalone-route rendering of these fields is t8's responsibility. Motivating evidence from s1 worth recording: a grep finds ZERO non-test commit producers, yet three tracked records carry body.commit (972bf31d, c90f3fe6, be8708a9) — back-filled BY HAND, showing the missing producer was felt and worked around rather than merely theoretical. Note the contrast with t5: here the SHORT sha from revParse is the right choice, because body.commit is a displayed reference rather than a range boundary.
acceptanceChecks: WRITE SIDE, both routes: a supplied summary reaches body.summary and body.commit is populated from HEAD, identically on the standalone and plan-driven routes
RENDER SIDE, PLAN-DRIVEN ONLY: body.summary renders as '## Summary' and body.commit as '**Commit:**'. Standalone-route rendering of both is asserted in t8, not here
An empty, whitespace-only or absent summary OMITS the key entirely rather than storing an empty string, and renders no section
body.commit is OMITTED — not empty-stringed — when HEAD cannot be read; revParse returns '' on failure, so the caller must treat '' as absent
A build that supplies no summary produces a record with no summary key — never synthesised, never invented from the task list

The dead-branch premise is pinned from the other direction: body.commit is now populated AUTOMATICALLY where previously it required hand-editing, with the three hand-filled records cited as the motivating evidence
The validate input's new field is OPTIONAL: a controller that never supplies it sees no behavioural difference
